attachment.snippet:
1	# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
6	2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
7	`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
8	roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
9	(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
10	access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.
11	
12	Two things block a sync:
13	
14	1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
15	   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
16	   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
17	   nothing durable can carry a group.
18	2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
19	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
20	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
21	   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
22	   job to reuse any of it.
23	
24	## Approach
25	
26	Six new or reshaped collections, one shared queue in a new infrastructure package, and one new
27	Cloud Run job inside the CRM app.
28	
29	### Schema (`packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/`)
30	
31	**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
32	`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name` and gains `google_group_id`.
33	`sessions`, `classes`, `registrations`, and `custom_field_definitions` repoint their `program_id` FK
34	to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs.
35	
36	Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
37	offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
38	never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
39	set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.
40	
41	**`google_groups`** — one row per Google Group: `email`, `name`, `settings_template`, `parent_id` self-FK.
42	`programs.google_group_id` points at the program group. `classes.google_group_id` points at the class group and is
43	set per offering. Non-program groups (`all@`, `staff@`) live here too, replacing the GAM "Group
44	Templates" worksheet (`gam/scripts/apply-templates:8`).
45	
46	**`program_roles`** — `person_id`, `program_id`, `role_id`, nullable `starts_on`/`ends_on`.
47	Separate from `event_staff` (`schema.yaml:140-166`): `event_staff` is person-plus-session and
48	Clubspot-derived, this is person-plus-program and hand-entered. Mixing sync-owned and hand-entered
49	rows in one collection is exactly the trap #137 describes.
50	
51	**`program_role_types`** — `name`, `grants_group_manager` boolean. `program_roles.role_id` points
52	here rather than at a schema enum, so adding a volunteer role is data entry, not a deploy. Seeded
53	with the two roles `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today, Parent Coordinator
54	and Group Manager, both granting manager.
55	
56	These are **not** `directus_roles`. A Directus role is an auth role: it decides what an API caller
57	may read and write, it is global rather than per-program, and it is IaC-managed in
58	`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts`. A parent coordinator is a
59	relationship between a person and a program, held mostly by people with no Directus login at all
60	(`people.directus_user_id` is nullable and usually null). Pointing at `directus_roles` would not
61	even remove a column — `program_id` still has to live on the join row — while it would add auth
62	roles that grant nothing and blur the authentication/authorization split `docs/architecture.md`
63	keeps deliberate. If a volunteer later needs to sign in, they get a Directus role *as well*, which
64	is the correct relationship between the two.

2. Most coordinators have no login at all — `people.directus_user_id` is nullable and usually null. A role pointing at an identity that does not exist is meaningless.
3. It would mean creating auth roles that grant nothing, which blurs the authentication/authorization split `docs/architecture.md` keeps deliberate.

But I think the real objection is the hardcoded enum, and that part is fair. So `role_id` now points at a small staff-maintained `program_role_types` collection — `name` plus a `grants_group_manager` boolean, seeded with the two roles the bash script hardcodes today. Adding a volunteer role becomes data entry rather than a deploy, and `grants_group_manager` puts the group-manager mapping in data instead of in `update-groups-from-roles`.

If your intent was that these volunteers will eventually log in, say so — they would then get a Directus role **as well**, which is the correct relationship between the two, not a replacement for this.

content.text:
PR #144 updated — `e9f5d5f3`, with inline replies on all four threads.

**Two I just did as asked:**

1. **`google_groups`** — collection renamed, FKs are `programs.google_group_id` and `classes.google_group_id`. "Group" was genuinely overloaded here.
2. **Queue and `DirectusClient` move out of `crm`** into a new `packages/directus`. You're right and `packages/crm/README.md:3` already said so in its own words — "Directus is the engine, not the app" — and I let it through anyway. Knock-on: `sync_tasks` gets applied by the **`infrastructure`** Pulumi project rather than `crm`, since that project already owns the Directus instance, its roles and users. No fourth project needed. The one wart is the name colliding with `packages/infrastructure/src/directus/` (the Pulumi resource classes) — free to rename now if you'd rather.

**One I pushed back on:**

3. **Directus roles for `program_roles`** — I don't think so, and the doc now argues it. A Directus role is an auth role: global, IaC-managed, decides API access. A parent coordinator is a person-program relationship, usually held by someone with no login (`people.directus_user_id` is nullable and mostly null). The FK removes no column either — `program_id` still lives on the join row — so it'd just swap an enum string for a role id while adding auth roles that grant nothing.

   But the hardcoded-enum objection is fair, so `role_id` now points at a small `program_role_types` collection: `name` plus `grants_group_manager`. Adding a volunteer role becomes data entry instead of a deploy, and the group-manager mapping moves out of the bash script into data. Overrule me if your intent was that these volunteers will eventually log in.

**One that needs your decision:**

4. **The job in `packages/crm`** — done, but it breaks a stated rule. `clubspot-sync` depends on `crm`, so once `crm` depends on `gsuite`, clubspot-sync gets Google transitively — and CLAUDE.md says clubspot-sync has "no gsuite dependency, by design". Options: accept it and reword the rule as code-level; fold `clubspot-sync` into `crm` too (consistent, and probably where this is heading, but much bigger than this batch); or keep the job as its own package. The doc assumes the first. It's in the doc as a blockquote so you can't miss it on re-read.

The worktree is back on `session/groups-sync` with the WIP commit intact. Implementation still paused.

Ultimately, our data model should be canonical, and anything saas-provider-specific should be explicit. So, I want to be able to capture the idea that "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed Program" and then map that to Google groups and directus roles as needed. 4. Update Claude - I don't think "no gsuite dependency, by design" is really still relevant, nor is a transitive dependency a problem.  Maybe we should consider a gsuite-sync package for the job. content.thinking:
This is a real architectural reframing to absorb: it's an integration platform where the CRM/Directus holds the canonical data model, and each SaaS provider gets a sync package mapping to/from that canonical model, with provider-specific quirks made explicit rather than hidden.

But I notice the CRM package currently has Clubspot-specific fields like clubspot_camp_id scattered throughout, which contradicts the canonical/provider split. The fix: `program_roles`/`program_role_types` stays canonical since it represents domain concepts like "Parent Coordinator," but something like `grants_group_manager` is really a Google Workspace-specific mapping rule and shouldn't live on the canonical model at all—it belongs in the gsuite-sync package's mapping logic instead.

So I'm weighing whether that mapping should be a TypeScript lookup table (simple but requires redeploys to change) versus a proper database collection like `google_group_role_mappings` that's data-driven and explicitly named as Google-specific, which fits the user's principle better. This same logic extends to `programs.google_group_id`—putting that FK directly on canonical entities is a leak, and the mapping should instead live in the Google-specific junction table.

Flipping the FK direction feels right: instead of canonical tables pointing to Google, `google_groups` should have nullable `program_id` and `class_id` fields pointing outward, so groups can represent a program, a class, or neither, and the canonical tables stay completely free of Google-specific structure. I'm now working through the query implications, since looking up "which group belongs to this class" becomes a reverse lookup rather than a forward FK, though Directus should handle that fine with an O2M alias.

The same reasoning applies to Clubspot IDs like `clubspot_camp_id` — under this principle they'd move into a dedicated mapping collection too, but that's a much larger refactor touching all of clubspot-sync. I want to flag it as the logical endpoint of this pattern without folding it into the current batch, and I'm also weighing a real counterargument: those IDs might just be natural keys from the system of record rather than something that needs to be abstracted away.

I land on a pragmatic split — external IDs stay on the row since they're cheap provenance data, but provider-specific behavior and structure get their own collections. This feels like a decision the user should weigh in on given how architecturally significant it is, and then I move to point 4, updating CLAUDE.md to remove the "no gsuite dependency, by design" note since a transitive dependency isn't actually a concern here.

For the gsuite sync job, I'm now thinking it deserves its own `packages/gsuite-sync` package rather than living inside crm — reversing the earlier comment on this. That fits a cleaner framing where CRM is the canonical app domain built on directus, and each sync job maps a SaaS product onto one or more app domains. Sketching the resulting package layout with directus as infrastructure, crm as the pure schema/domain package, and separate sync/SDK packages per provider like clubspot.

This structure is symmetric and clean — crm reverts to being just schema and types with no gsuite dependency, which actually dissolves the CLAUDE.md conflict they were asking me to resolve. I'm double-checking this holds: if both gsuite-sync and clubspot-sync depend on crm plus their own provider SDK, crm stays free of any gsuite dependency and clubspot-sync doesn't inherit anything unwanted transitively, so the dependency rule is preserved structurally.

The user explicitly said they want to think more about point 3 before implementing, so I shouldn't push a solution — instead I should offer a clean framing (canonical vs provider-specific, where the boundary sits) without editing the doc's role modeling yet. They've already hinted at their own direction: the data model should stay canonical, with anything provider-specific made explicit, so something like "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed Program" maps outward to Google Groups and other systems rather than being defined by them.

That points toward a shape where `program_role_types` stays canonical and provider-specific bits like `grants_group_manager` move into a separate mapping table, with similar mappings eventually needed for Directus roles too. I could flag the bigger open questions here — like whether canonical rows need external IDs, or how `programs.google_group_id` should point — as things worth thinking through, along with a recommendation.

I'm noticing something worth naming explicitly: Directus isn't just the canonical store, it's also itself a provider with its own users and roles, which is why `people.directus_user_id` already lives as a provider-specific column on a canonical table. Now I need to figure out the concrete next steps — updating CLAUDE.md would fit under a later step involving the package list and dependency graph, but that file lives on main and the session branch rather than the docs-only plan branch, so I shouldn't touch it here.

Since editing CLAUDE.md directly would turn the plan PR into something more than a plan, I'll just document the change under that later step and defer the actual edit to implementation time, rather than trying to sneak it into the session branch now.

I still have a few more items to line up: reintroducing the gsuite-sync package instead of folding it into crm, splitting canonical vs provider-specific fields in the role model, and flagging the broader architectural question for later consideration. I'm also thinking the doc deserves a short "Architecture" section laying out the integration-platform principle, since that framing ties all these decisions together and future work will reference it — worth adding a few lines. Time to switch back to the plan branch and start making these edits.

On the direction question for `programs.google_group_id` vs. `google_groups.program_id`, I'm weighing keeping provider-specific columns out of the canonical tables (so adding Slack later doesn't force a `slack_channel_id` onto `programs`) against the simplicity of querying directly from the canonical side and how the Directus UI would handle editing.

The scaling argument settles it: reverse FKs, where each provider table owns its mapping, avoid piling on a new column per provider as they multiply. The UI concern is moot too, since Directus can expose this via an O2M alias field on `programs`, the same pattern `my_contacts` already uses. Time to switch to the plan branch and write out the edits.

## The shape this fits into

This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:

```text
packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
```

The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
SaaS product is named for that product.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed
program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google Group" is a

> not have. A program group must not be used as an oauth2-proxy allowlist (#65, #98) until that is

**Managers and owners**: managers come from `program_roles` rows that are current on the run date.
Owners come from a config list of the break-glass super-admins — `master@` today, `commander@` once
#81 lands.

**Audit**: one pass per run compares live membership and settings against the plan and writes
`audit_findings` rows for the differences. It never removes anyone.

### Auth and infrastructure

The job runs as a new `groups-sync-runner` service account
(`packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap/groups-sync.ts`, mirroring `bootstrap/clubspot-sync.ts:6`).
Writing groups needs `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group` and
`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.groups.settings` — both wider than the read-only scope the
substrate holds today (`docs/manual-setup.md:99-101`), so this is a separate identity, not a reuse of
`substrate-runner`.


Directus access is a second static token with its own machine user, following
`clubspot-sync-directus-token` (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus.ts:62`). Its
policy is read on `people`, `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `classes`,
`offerings`, `programs`, `google_groups`, `program_roles`, and write on `sync_tasks` and `audit_findings`
only. No GCP project roles. Nothing changes in `config.ts` — this identity is not a deployer.

### What can be tested

Settled with the user before implementation started.

- **An offering is linked to its program by hand**, once per offering, roughly a dozen times a year.
  Rejected a `program_matchers` pattern table: more code, and it silently mislinks a renamed camp.
- **A program gets a group only if `google_group_id` is set.** There is no other rule. `program_without_group`
  makes the omission visible instead of silent.
- **Groups are for discussion.** Members post to lists they belong to. Listmonk still gets its own
  list sync later for the newsletter (#71), reading the same CRM.
- **Group owners are config constants**, not CRM data — `master@` today, `commander@` once #81 lands.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
6	2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
7	`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
8	roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
9	(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
10	access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.
11	
12	Two things block a sync:
13	
14	1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
15	   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
16	   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
17	   nothing durable can carry a group.
18	2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
19	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
20	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
21	   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
22	   job to reuse any of it.
23	
24	## The shape this fits into
25	
26	This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
27	product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:
28	
29	```text
30	packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
31	packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
32	packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
33	packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
34	```
35	
36	The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
37	SaaS product is named for that product.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed
38	program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google Group" is a
39	Google Workspace mapping and lives in a `google_`-prefixed collection. The same role later maps to
40	a Directus policy through its own mapping, without the canonical row changing.
41	
42	Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
43	which is why `people.directus_user_id` is already a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
44	
45	## Approach
46	
47	Seven new or reshaped collections, one shared queue in a new infrastructure package, and one new
48	sync package.
49	
50	### Schema (`packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/`)
51	
52	**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
53	`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name` and gains
54	`google_group_id`. `sessions`, `classes`, `registrations`, and `custom_field_definitions` repoint
55	their `program_id` FK to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual Directus edits exist and all data
56	re-syncs.
57	
58	Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
59	offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
60	never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
61	set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.
62

1	# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
6	2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
7	`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
8	roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
9	(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
10	access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.
11	
12	Two things block a sync:
13	
14	1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
15	   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
16	   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
17	   nothing durable can carry a group.
18	2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
19	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
20	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
21	   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
22	   job to reuse any of it.
23	
24	## The shape this fits into
25	
26	This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
27	product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:
28	
29	```text
30	packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
31	packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
32	packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
33	packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
34	```
35	
36	The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
37	SaaS product is named for that product.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed
38	program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google Group" is a
39	Google Workspace mapping and lives in a `google_`-prefixed collection. The same role later maps to
40	a Directus policy through its own mapping, without the canonical row changing.
41	
42	Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
43	which is why `people.directus_user_id` is already a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
44	
45	## Approach
46	
47	Seven new or reshaped collections, one shared queue in a new infrastructure package, and one new
48	sync package.
49	
50	### Schema
51	
52	Applying the rule above, the new collections land in three schemas, each owned by the package that
53	owns the concern:
54	
55	| Schema                        | Collections                                            |
56	| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
57	| `crm` (canonical)             | `programs`, `offerings`, `program_roles`, `program_role_types` |
58	| `directus` (infrastructure)   | `sync_tasks`, `audit_findings`                         |
59	| `gsuite-sync` (provider)      | `google_groups`, `google_group_roles`                  |
60	
61	`audit_findings` sits with the queue rather than with Google because every sync will want one —
62	`unlinked_offering` is already a Clubspot finding, not a Google one. The Directus instance is
63	shared and each package applies its own schema, which is the model
64	`packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:9-12` already describes.
65	
66	**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
67	`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name` and gains nothing —
68	the Google Group that represents it points the other way. `sessions`, `classes`, `registrations`,
69	and `custom_field_definitions` repoint their `program_id` FK to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual
70	Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs.
71	
72	Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
73	offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
74	never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
75	set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.
76	
77	**`google_groups`** (provider) — one row per Google Group: `email`, `name`, `settings_template`,
78	`parent_id` self-FK, plus nullable `program_id` and `class_id` saying which canonical thing this
79	group represents. Non-program groups (`all@`, `staff@`) leave both null and live here too,
80	replacing the GAM "Group Templates" worksheet (`gam/scripts/apply-templates:8`).
81	
82	The mapping points **from** the provider table **to** the canonical one, not the reverse. A
83	`programs.google_group_id` column would mean a `programs.slack_channel_id` when the next provider
84	arrives, and a canonical table that grows a column per SaaS product. This way each provider owns
85	its own mapping and the canonical tables never change. Uniqueness on `class_id` is what enforces
86	one group per class. Staff still see the group on a program's detail page — an O2M alias field,
87	the same trick `my_contacts` already uses on `people`.
88	
89	**`program_roles`** — `person_id`, `program_id`, `role_id`, nullable `starts_on`/`ends_on`.
90	Separate from `event_staff` (`schema.yaml:140-166`): `event_staff` is person-plus-session and
91	Clubspot-derived, this is person-plus-program and hand-entered. Mixing sync-owned and hand-entered
92	rows in one collection is exactly the trap #137 describes.
93	
94	**`program_role_types`** (canonical) — just `name`. `program_roles.role_id` points here rather
95	than at a schema enum, so adding a volunteer role is data entry, not a deploy. Seeded with the two
96	roles `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today: Parent Coordinator and Group
97	Manager. It carries no provider behaviour — "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of Double-handed" is the
98	whole of what it says.
99	
100	**`google_group_roles`** (provider) — `program_role_type_id`, `google_role` (`MEMBER`, `MANAGER`,
101	`OWNER`). The mapping that today is hardcoded in `update-groups-from-roles:38-51`. Both seeded
102	roles map to `MANAGER`. A role with no row here simply has no effect on Google Groups.
103	
104	Neither is `directus_roles`. A Directus role is an auth role: global rather than per-program,
105	IaC-managed in `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts`, and it decides what
106	an API caller may read and write. A parent coordinator is a person-program relationship, held
107	mostly by people with no login at all (`people.directus_user_id` is nullable and usually null).
108	When these roles do need to grant Directus access, that gets its own mapping collection alongside
109	`google_group_roles` — the same pattern, a different provider — rather than collapsing the
110	canonical role into the auth one.
111	
112	**`audit_findings`** — `kind` (`unexpected_member`, `settings_drift`, `missing_group`,
113	`unlinked_offering`, `program_without_group`), `group_email`, `detail`, `status` (`open`,
114	`dismissed`). Staff dismiss a row and the dismissal persists across runs, so a finding needs a
115	stable identity the next run can recognise — `kind` plus `group_email` plus a hash of `detail`,
116	carried in a unique `fingerprint` column. Without it a dismissed finding returns on the next pass.
117	No Google Sheet, so the job needs no Sheets dependency. Possible home for a review UI later
118	(#133).
119	
120	**`sync_tasks`** — the durable queue: `queue`, `kind`, `key`, `parent_id` self-FK, `status`,
121	`attempts`, `max_attempts`, `run_after`, `last_error`, `started_at`, `finished_at`. `key` is the
122	target's natural key, so a re-enqueue updates a pending task instead of piling up. A task may enqueue

1	# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
6	2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
7	`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
8	roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
9	(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
10	access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.
11	
12	Two things block a sync:
13	
14	1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
15	   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
16	   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
17	   nothing durable can carry a group.
18	2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
19	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
20	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
21	   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
22	   job to reuse any of it.
23	
24	## The shape this fits into
25	
26	This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
27	product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:
28	
29	```text
30	packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
31	packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
32	packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
33	packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
34	```
35	
36	The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
37	SaaS product is named for that product.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed
38	program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google Group" is a
39	Google Workspace mapping and lives in a `google_`-prefixed collection. The same role later maps to
40	a Directus policy through its own mapping, without the canonical row changing.
41	
42	Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
43	which is why `people.directus_user_id` is already a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
44	
45	## Approach
46	
47	Seven new or reshaped collections, one shared queue in a new infrastructure package, and one new
48	sync package.
49	
50	### Schema
51	
52	Applying the rule above, the new collections land in three schemas, each owned by the package that
53	owns the concern:
54	
55	| Schema                      | Collections                                                    |
56	| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
57	| `crm` (canonical)           | `programs`, `offerings`, `program_roles`, `program_role_types` |
58	| `directus` (infrastructure) | `sync_tasks`, `audit_findings`                                 |
59	| `gsuite-sync` (provider)    | `google_groups`, `google_group_roles`                          |
60	
61	`audit_findings` sits with the queue rather than with Google because every sync will want one —
62	`unlinked_offering` is already a Clubspot finding, not a Google one. The Directus instance is
63	shared and each package applies its own schema, which is the model
64	`packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:9-12` already describes.
65	
66	**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
67	`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name` and gains nothing —
68	the Google Group that represents it points the other way. `sessions`, `classes`, `registrations`,
69	and `custom_field_definitions` repoint their `program_id` FK to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual
70	Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs.
71	
72	Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
73	offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
74	never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
75	set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.
76	
77	**`google_groups`** (provider) — one row per Google Group: `email`, `name`, `settings_template`,
78	`parent_id` self-FK, plus nullable `program_id` and `class_id` saying which canonical thing this
79	group represents. Non-program groups (`all@`, `staff@`) leave both null and live here too,
80	replacing the GAM "Group Templates" worksheet (`gam/scripts/apply-templates:8`).
81	
82	The mapping points **from** the provider table **to** the canonical one, not the reverse. A
83	`programs.google_group_id` column would mean a `programs.slack_channel_id` when the next provider
84	arrives, and a canonical table that grows a column per SaaS product. This way each provider owns
85	its own mapping and the canonical tables never change. Uniqueness on `class_id` is what enforces
86	one group per class. Staff still see the group on a program's detail page — an O2M alias field,
87	the same trick `my_contacts` already uses on `people`.
88	
89	**`program_roles`** — `person_id`, `program_id`, `role_id`, nullable `starts_on`/`ends_on`.
90	Separate from `event_staff` (`schema.yaml:140-166`): `event_staff` is person-plus-session and
91	Clubspot-derived, this is person-plus-program and hand-entered. Mixing sync-owned and hand-entered
92	rows in one collection is exactly the trap #137 describes.
93	
94	**`program_role_types`** (canonical) — just `name`. `program_roles.role_id` points here rather
95	than at a schema enum, so adding a volunteer role is data entry, not a deploy. Seeded with the two
96	roles `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today: Parent Coordinator and Group
97	Manager. It carries no provider behaviour — "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of Double-handed" is the
98	whole of what it says.
99	
100	**`google_group_roles`** (provider) — `program_role_type_id`, `google_role` (`MEMBER`, `MANAGER`,
101	`OWNER`). The mapping that today is hardcoded in `update-groups-from-roles:38-51`. Both seeded
102	roles map to `MANAGER`. A role with no row here simply has no effect on Google Groups.
103	
104	Neither is `directus_roles`. A Directus role is an auth role: global rather than per-program,
105	IaC-managed in `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts`, and it decides what
106	an API caller may read and write. A parent coordinator is a person-program relationship, held
107	mostly by people with no login at all (`people.directus_user_id` is nullable and usually null).
108	When these roles do need to grant Directus access, that gets its own mapping collection alongside
109	`google_group_roles` — the same pattern, a different provider — rather than collapsing the
110	canonical role into the auth one.
111	
112	**`audit_findings`** (infrastructure) — `source` (which sync raised it), `kind`, `subject` (what
113	it is about, a group address here), `detail`, `status` (`open`, `dismissed`). Kinds this work
114	raises: `unexpected_member`, `settings_drift`, `missing_group`, `unlinked_offering`,
115	`program_without_group`. Staff dismiss a row and the dismissal persists across runs, so a finding
116	needs a stable identity the next run can recognise — `source` plus `kind` plus `subject` plus a
117	hash of `detail`, carried in a unique `fingerprint` column. Without it a dismissed finding returns
118	on the next pass. No Google Sheet, so the job needs no Sheets dependency. Possible home for a
119	review UI later (#133).
120	
121	**`sync_tasks`** — the durable queue: `queue`, `kind`, `key`, `parent_id` self-FK, `status`,
122	`attempts`, `max_attempts`, `run_after`, `last_error`, `started_at`, `finished_at`. `key` is the

Reframed the whole doc around the integration-platform framing. `b6eb90f9`.

There is a new section at the top, **The shape this fits into**, stating the rule so it outlives this work: *a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one SaaS product is named for that product.* Step 10 now copies that rule into CLAUDE.md.

**On 4 — `packages/gsuite-sync`, not inside `crm`.** Google Workspace's side of the platform, mirroring `clubspot-sync` on Clubspot's. Groups today; Workspace users or shared drives later go here rather than in a third package. Worth noting this dissolves the dependency problem on its own — `crm` goes back to being schema-and-types with no jobs and no `gsuite` dependency, so nothing reaches `clubspot-sync` transitively. The "no gsuite dependency, by design" note still gets dropped in step 10, since the boundary that matters is one provider per sync package, not a transitive import.

**On 3 — the canonical/provider split, applied.** `program_role_types` is now canonical and carries *only* a name. "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of Double-handed" is the whole of what it says. The Google behaviour moved out to `google_group_roles` (`program_role_type_id` → `MEMBER`/`MANAGER`/`OWNER`), which is the mapping `update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today. A Directus-policy mapping later is the same pattern with a different provider.

Two consequences I applied for consistency, both worth a look since they go further than your comment:

1. **The group→canonical FK reversed direction.** `google_groups` now carries nullable `program_id` and `class_id` instead of `programs.google_group_id`. Otherwise every canonical table grows a column per SaaS product. Staff still see the group on a program's detail page via an O2M alias, the same trick `my_contacts` uses.
2. **Three schemas instead of one**, each owned by the package that owns the concern: `crm` canonical, `directus` infrastructure (`sync_tasks` + `audit_findings`), `gsuite-sync` provider. `audit_findings` moved to infrastructure and got a `source` column, because `unlinked_offering` is a Clubspot finding, not a Google one.

**The question I could not settle for you** is now open question 1: the principle applied strictly also condemns `offerings.clubspot_camp_id`, `sessions.clubspot_session_id`, and `people.directus_user_id` — provider columns on canonical tables, all pre-existing.

My recommendation is to draw the line at **structure and behaviour, not identity**. An external id is provenance: the row would not exist without it, and hoisting it into a side table costs a join on every upsert in the sync hot path for no behavioural gain. Provider structure (the group graph) and provider behaviour (which Google role a volunteer gets) do earn their own collections. If you want the strict version it is a separate piece of work across every sync, not something to fold in here.

Pushed `b6eb90f9` with a summary comment on the PR.

**The framing is now a section at the top of the doc**, so it outlives this work, and step 10 copies it into CLAUDE.md:

```
packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new)
```

**On 4** — `packages/gsuite-sync`. Worth noting it dissolves the dependency question on its own: `crm` goes back to schema-and-types with no jobs and no `gsuite`, so nothing reaches `clubspot-sync` transitively. The CLAUDE.md note still gets dropped, since the boundary that matters is one provider per sync package.

**On 3** — `program_role_types` is canonical and carries only a name. Google behaviour moved to `google_group_roles` (`program_role_type_id` → `MEMBER`/`MANAGER`/`OWNER`), which is exactly the mapping `update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today. A Directus-policy mapping later is the same pattern, different provider.

**Two things I took further than you asked**, because the principle seemed to demand it — push back if I overreached:

1. **The group FK reversed.** `google_groups` carries nullable `program_id`/`class_id`, rather than `programs.google_group_id`. Otherwise every canonical table grows a column per SaaS product. The Directus UI still shows the group on a program via an O2M alias, same as `my_contacts`.
2. **Three schemas, not one** — `crm` canonical, `directus` infrastructure, `gsuite-sync` provider. `audit_findings` moved to infrastructure with a `source` column, since `unlinked_offering` is a Clubspot finding and not a Google one.

**What I couldn't settle for you** is now open question 1. Applied strictly, the principle also condemns `offerings.clubspot_camp_id`, `sessions.clubspot_session_id`, and `people.directus_user_id` — all pre-existing provider columns on canonical tables. My recommendation is to draw the line at **structure and behaviour, not identity**: an external id is provenance, the row wouldn't exist without it, and hoisting it into a side table costs a join on every upsert in the sync hot path for no behavioural gain. If you want the strict version, that's separate work across every sync.

Implementation still paused; the worktree is back on `session/groups-sync` with the WIP commit intact.

+This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS

The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
SaaS product is named for that product.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed
program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google Group" is a
Google Workspace mapping and lives in a `google_`-prefixed collection. The same role later maps to
a Directus policy through its own mapping, without the canonical row changing.

Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
which is why `people.directus_user_id` is already a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
input.new_string:
The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
SaaS product is owned by that product's package.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the
Double-handed program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google
Group" is a Google Workspace mapping. The same role later maps to a Directus policy through its
own mapping, without the canonical row changing.

Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
which is why `people.directus_user_id` is a provider-specific column on a canonical table.

### Providers extend canonical collections

Ownership is about **which schema declares a thing**, not about which table it sits on. A provider
may add a field to a canonical collection: `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on
`programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema, not in `crm`'s. Staff see it where they expect it,
and the canonical package still knows nothing about Google.

The machinery for this already half exists. `scopeSnapshot`
(`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is what makes "my schema does not
mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X" (#109). It is
**collection-granular** today: `owned` is a set of collection names and every live entry under
them is replaced. It needs to become field-granular — `owned` splits into collections this package
owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection, with `fields` and
`relations` filtered on both. The comment at `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a
relation is always a collection this app owns; extension fields break that and it needs rewording.

Consequences, all mild:

- Provider schemas apply **after** the canonical one, since the collection must exist first. The
  justfile already orders projects.
- `just directus-local` must apply every package's schema, not only `packages/crm/schema.yaml`.
- Permission rules are collection-level, so a provider's field on `programs` is already covered by
  the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
- Row types do not compose automatically: `ProgramRow` in `crm` will not carry `google_group_id`.
  Consumers that need both intersect the two types.

1	# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
6	2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
7	`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
8	roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
9	(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
10	access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.
11	
12	Two things block a sync:
13	
14	1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
15	   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
16	   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
17	   nothing durable can carry a group.
18	2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
19	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
20	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
21	   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
22	   job to reuse any of it.
23	
24	## The shape this fits into
25	
26	This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
27	product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:
28	
29	```text
30	packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
31	packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
32	packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
33	packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
34	```
35	
36	The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
37	SaaS product is owned by that product's package.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the
38	Double-handed program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google
39	Group" is a Google Workspace mapping. The same role later maps to a Directus policy through its
40	own mapping, without the canonical row changing.
41	
42	Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
43	which is why `people.directus_user_id` is a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
44	
45	### Providers extend canonical collections
46	
47	Ownership is about **which schema declares a thing**, not about which table it sits on. A provider
48	may add a field to a canonical collection: `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on
49	`programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema, not in `crm`'s. Staff see it where they expect it,
50	and the canonical package still knows nothing about Google.
51	
52	The machinery for this already half exists. `scopeSnapshot`
53	(`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is what makes "my schema does not
54	mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X" (#109). It is
55	**collection-granular** today: `owned` is a set of collection names and every live entry under
56	them is replaced. It needs to become field-granular — `owned` splits into collections this package
57	owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection, with `fields` and
58	`relations` filtered on both. The comment at `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a
59	relation is always a collection this app owns; extension fields break that and it needs rewording.
60	
61	Consequences, all mild:
62	
63	- Provider schemas apply **after** the canonical one, since the collection must exist first. The
64	  justfile already orders projects.
65	- `just directus-local` must apply every package's schema, not only `packages/crm/schema.yaml`.
66	- Permission rules are collection-level, so a provider's field on `programs` is already covered by
67	  the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
68	- Row types do not compose automatically: `ProgramRow` in `crm` will not carry `google_group_id`.
69	  Consumers that need both intersect the two types.
70	
71	## Approach
72	
73	Seven new or reshaped collections, one shared queue in a new infrastructure package, and one new
74	sync package.
75	
76	### Schema
77	
78	Applying the rule above, the new collections land in three schemas, each owned by the package that
79	owns the concern:
80	
81	| Schema                      | Owns                                                                            |
82	| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
83	| `crm` (canonical)           | `programs`, `offerings`, `program_roles`, `program_role_types`                  |
84	| `directus` (infrastructure) | `sync_tasks`, `audit_findings`                                                  |
85	| `gsuite-sync` (provider)    | `google_groups`, `google_group_roles`, and the fields `programs.google_group_id` and `classes.google_group_id` |
86	
87	`audit_findings` sits with the queue rather than with Google because every sync will want one —
88	`unlinked_offering` is already a Clubspot finding, not a Google one. The Directus instance is
89	shared and each package applies its own schema, which is the model
90	`packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:9-12` already describes.
91	
92	**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
93	`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name`; its
94	`google_group_id` is a `gsuite-sync` extension field, not a `crm` one. `sessions`, `classes`,
95	`registrations`,
96	and `custom_field_definitions` repoint their `program_id` FK to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual
97	Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs.
98	
99	Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
100	offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
101	never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
102	set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.
103	
104	**`google_groups`** (provider) — one row per Google Group: `email`, `name`, `settings_template`,
105	`parent_id` self-FK. Non-program groups (`all@`, `staff@`) live here too, replacing the GAM "Group
106	Templates" worksheet (`gam/scripts/apply-templates:8`).
107	
108	**`programs.google_group_id` and `classes.google_group_id`** (provider extension fields) — FKs on
109	the canonical collections, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema per the section above. The class one
110	is set per offering. Nullable: a program or class with no group is the normal case.
111	
112	**`program_roles`** — `person_id`, `program_id`, `role_id`, nullable `starts_on`/`ends_on`.
113	Separate from `event_staff` (`schema.yaml:140-166`): `event_staff` is person-plus-session and
114	Clubspot-derived, this is person-plus-program and hand-entered. Mixing sync-owned and hand-entered
115	rows in one collection is exactly the trap #137 describes.
116

- **Groups are for discussion.** Members post to lists they belong to. Listmonk still gets its own
  list sync later for the newsletter (#71), reading the same CRM.
- **Group owners are config constants**, not CRM data — `master@` today, `commander@` once #81 lands.
  Ownership is a break-glass boundary and should not be editable from the admin UI.

## Open questions

1. **How far does "canonical, with providers explicit" go?** This doc applies it to the new
   collections. It does not apply it to the ones that already exist: `offerings.clubspot_camp_id`,
   `sessions.clubspot_session_id`, `registrations.clubspot_registration_id`, and
   `people.directus_user_id` are all provider-specific columns on canonical tables.

   Recommendation — draw the line at **structure and behaviour, not identity**. An external id is
   provenance: the row would not exist without it, Clubspot is the system of record for that row,
   and hoisting it into a `clubspot_offerings` side table buys purity at the cost of a join on
   every upsert in the hot path. Provider _behaviour_ (which Google role a volunteer gets) and
   provider _structure_ (the group graph) do get their own collections, which is what this doc
   does. If you want the stricter version, it is a separate piece of work across every sync, not
   something to fold in here.

2. **Does the Groups Settings API accept a service-account role assignment?** Unknown, and the only
   thing gating the settings and settings-drift passes. Test before step 7; fall back to leaving
   settings with `gam/scripts/apply-templates`.

3. **Create `packages/directus`:** move `DirectusClient` into it, add `sync_tasks` and
   `audit_findings` in its own schema, the queue planner, the worker, and unit tests. Apply the
   schema from the `infrastructure` Pulumi project.
4. **Move `clubspot-sync` onto the queue.** Delete `sync-log.ts`, drop `sync_runs` /
   `sync_program_runs`, add `offerings.synced_through` and `offerings.quiet_runs`, and rewrite

6. **Create `packages/gsuite-sync`** with its `google_groups` / `google_group_roles` schema and the

attachment.snippet:
1	# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
6	2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
7	`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
8	roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
9	(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
10	access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.
11	
12	Two things block a sync:
13	
14	1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
15	   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
16	   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
17	   nothing durable can carry a group.
18	2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
19	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
20	   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
21	   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
22	   job to reuse any of it.
23	
24	## The shape this fits into
25	
26	This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
27	product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:
28	
29	```text
30	packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
31	packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
32	packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
33	packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
34	```
35	
36	The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
37	SaaS product is owned by that product's package.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the
38	Double-handed program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google
39	Group" is a Google Workspace mapping. The same role later maps to a Directus policy through its
40	own mapping, without the canonical row changing.
41	
42	Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
43	which is why `people.directus_user_id` is a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
44	
45	### Providers extend canonical collections
46	
47	Ownership is about **which schema declares a thing**, not about which table it sits on. A provider
48	may add a field to a canonical collection: `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on
49	`programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema, not in `crm`'s. Staff see it where they expect it,
50	and the canonical package still knows nothing about Google.
51	
52	The machinery for this already half exists. `scopeSnapshot`
53	(`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is what makes "my schema does not
54	mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X" (#109). It is
55	**collection-granular** today: `owned` is a set of collection names and every live entry under
56	them is replaced. It needs to become field-granular — `owned` splits into collections this package
57	owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection, with `fields` and
58	`relations` filtered on both. The comment at `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a
59	relation is always a collection this app owns; extension fields break that and it needs rewording.
60	
61	Consequences, all mild:
62	
63	- Provider schemas apply **after** the canonical one, since the collection must exist first. The
64	  justfile already orders projects.
65	- `just directus-local` must apply every package's schema, not only `packages/crm/schema.yaml`.
66	- Permission rules are collection-level, so a provider's field on `programs` is already covered by
67	  the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
68	- Row types do not compose automatically: `ProgramRow` in `crm` will not carry `google_group_id`.
69	  Consumers that need both intersect the two types.
70	
71	## Approach
72	
73	Seven new or reshaped collections, one shared queue in a new infrastructure package, and one new
74	sync package.
75	
76	### Schema
77	
78	Applying the rule above, the new collections land in three schemas, each owned by the package that
79	owns the concern:
80	
81	| Schema                      | Owns                                                                            |
82	| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
83	| `crm` (canonical)           | `programs`, `offerings`, `program_roles`, `program_role_types`                  |
84	| `directus` (infrastructure) | `sync_tasks`, `audit_findings`                                                  |
85	| `gsuite-sync` (provider)    | `google_groups`, `google_group_roles`, and the fields `programs.google_group_id` and `classes.google_group_id` |
86	
87	`audit_findings` sits with the queue rather than with Google because every sync will want one —
88	`unlinked_offering` is already a Clubspot finding, not a Google one. The Directus instance is
89	shared and each package applies its own schema, which is the model
90	`packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:9-12` already describes.
91	
92	**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
93	`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name`; its
94	`google_group_id` is a `gsuite-sync` extension field, not a `crm` one. `sessions`, `classes`,
95	`registrations`,
96	and `custom_field_definitions` repoint their `program_id` FK to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual
97	Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs.
98	
99	Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
100	offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
101	never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
102	set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.
103	
104	**`google_groups`** (provider) — one row per Google Group: `email`, `name`, `settings_template`,
105	`parent_id` self-FK. Non-program groups (`all@`, `staff@`) live here too, replacing the GAM "Group
106	Templates" worksheet (`gam/scripts/apply-templates:8`).
107	
108	**`programs.google_group_id` and `classes.google_group_id`** (provider extension fields) — FKs on
109	the canonical collections, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema per the section above. The class one
110	is set per offering. Nullable: a program or class with no group is the normal case.
111	
112	**`program_roles`** — `person_id`, `program_id`, `role_id`, nullable `starts_on`/`ends_on`.
113	Separate from `event_staff` (`schema.yaml:140-166`): `event_staff` is person-plus-session and
114	Clubspot-derived, this is person-plus-program and hand-entered. Mixing sync-owned and hand-entered
115	rows in one collection is exactly the trap #137 describes.
116

input.content:
Adopted. `1bff1632`. You are right and my reversal was the wrong fix — it made Google clean at the cost of a rule that could not generalize, which is exactly the objection.

**Providers extend canonical collections.** New section in the doc. Ownership is about which schema *declares* a thing, not which table it sits on: `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on `programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema. The FK reversal is gone and `google_groups` is back to describing only the group.

**It is cheap, because half the machinery is already there.** `scopeSnapshot` (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is what makes "my schema does not mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X" — the #109 fix. It is **collection-granular**: `owned` is a set of collection names, and every live entry under them is replaced wholesale. It needs to become field-granular, with `owned` splitting into collections a package owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection. Roughly 30 lines plus tests in the existing `directus-client.test.ts`. That is now step 3, on its own, so step 7 is not debugging two new things at once.

Three things fall out of it, all good:

- **Permission rules are collection-level**, so a provider field on `programs` is already covered by the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
- **No data migrates, ever.** A column does not move table; only the file declaring it changes.
- **Open question 1 is closed**, and closed the way you wanted. The rule now applies to every provider, not just Google: the nine `clubspot_*` id columns move to `clubspot-sync`'s schema and `people.directus_user_id` to `directus`'s. That is step 11 — last, because it is a pure reorganization and should not be able to destabilize anything above it.

Two costs worth naming:

- One comment becomes wrong. `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a relation is always a collection this app owns. Extension fields break that; step 3 rewords it.
- Row types do not compose automatically. `ProgramRow` in `crm` will not carry `google_group_id`, so a consumer needing both intersects the two types. Mild, but it is the one place the seam shows in day-to-day code.

The only open question left is whether the Groups Settings API accepts a service-account role assignment, which gates step 8 alone and has a documented fallback.

content.text:
Adopted — `1bff1632`. You were right and my reversal was the wrong fix: it made Google clean at the cost of a rule that couldn't generalize, which is exactly what you objected to.

**Ownership is about which schema declares a thing, not which table it sits on.** `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on `programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema. The reversal is gone; `google_groups` is back to describing only the group.

**It's cheap, because half the machinery already exists.** `scopeSnapshot` (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is the #109 fix — what makes "my schema doesn't mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X". It's collection-granular: `owned` is a set of collection names and every live entry under them gets replaced wholesale. It needs to become field-granular, with `owned` splitting into collections a package owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection. ~30 lines plus tests in the existing `directus-client.test.ts`. That's now step 3 on its own, so step 7 isn't debugging two new things at once.

Three things fall out, all good:

- **Permission rules are collection-level**, so a provider field on `programs` is already covered by the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
- **Nothing ever migrates.** A column doesn't move table; only the declaring file changes.
- **Open question 1 closed, your way.** The rule now applies to every provider: the nine `clubspot_*` id columns move to `clubspot-sync`'s schema, `people.directus_user_id` to `directus`'s. That's step 11 — last, since a pure reorganization shouldn't be able to destabilize anything above it.

Two costs worth naming. One comment becomes wrong — `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a relation is always a collection this app owns, which extension fields break; step 3 rewords it. And row types don't compose: `ProgramRow` in `crm` won't carry `google_group_id`, so consumers needing both intersect the two types. Mild, but it's the one place the seam shows in everyday code.

Plan is now 12 steps. The only open question left is the Groups Settings API one, which gates step 8 alone and has a fallback. Worktree back on `session/groups-sync`, implementation still paused.

+## The shape this fits into
+This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
+product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:
+```text
+packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
+packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
+packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
+packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
+The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
+SaaS product is owned by that product's package.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the
+Double-handed program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google
+Group" is a Google Workspace mapping. The same role later maps to a Directus policy through its
+own mapping, without the canonical row changing.
+Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
+which is why `people.directus_user_id` is a provider-specific column on a canonical table.
+### Providers extend canonical collections
+Ownership is about **which schema declares a thing**, not about which table it sits on. A provider
+may add a field to a canonical collection: `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on
+`programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema, not in `crm`'s. Staff see it where they expect it,
+and the canonical package still knows nothing about Google.
+The machinery for this already half exists. `scopeSnapshot`
+(`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is what makes "my schema does not
+mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X" (#109). It is
+**collection-granular** today: `owned` is a set of collection names and every live entry under
+them is replaced. It needs to become field-granular — `owned` splits into collections this package
+owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection, with `fields` and
+`relations` filtered on both. The comment at `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a
+relation is always a collection this app owns; extension fields break that and it needs rewording.
+Consequences, all mild:
+- Provider schemas apply **after** the canonical one, since the collection must exist first. The
+  justfile already orders projects.
+- `just directus-local` must apply every package's schema, not only `packages/crm/schema.yaml`.
+- Permission rules are collection-level, so a provider's field on `programs` is already covered by
+  the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
+- Row types do not compose automatically: `ProgramRow` in `crm` will not carry `google_group_id`.
+  Consumers that need both intersect the two types.

Implements `.claude/plans/crm-to-google-groups-sync.md`, approved in the review threads above. Tracked by #143, carved out of #71.

## What this does

Group membership is maintained by hand today — `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts` hardcodes six `camp|class|group` mappings that get edited every season. This makes it a consequence of CRM data instead.

Three things land together, because the sync needs all of them:

1. **`programs` splits into durable `programs` + dated `offerings`.** A Clubspot Camp is an *instance* of a program. Breaking change; all CRM data re-syncs.
2. **A durable task queue** (`sync_tasks`) in a new `packages/directus`, with per-item retry and a backlog visible in the admin UI. Both syncs move onto it.
3. **`packages/gsuite-sync`**, a Cloud Run job that writes Google Groups from the CRM, add-only, with an audit pass that reports rather than removes.

## The framing it establishes

This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the canonical model; each SaaS product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains. Anything specific to one product is owned by that product's package — including fields it adds to canonical collections, which is what makes `programs.google_group_id` a `gsuite-sync` field on a `crm` collection. Step 12 records the rule in CLAUDE.md, since it outlives this work.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. Split `programs` into `programs` + `offerings`
- [ ] 2. Canonical `program_role_types` and `program_roles`
- [ ] 3. Make `scopeSnapshot` field-granular so providers can extend canonical collections
- [ ] 4. `packages/directus`: `DirectusClient`, `sync_tasks`, `audit_findings`, queue and worker
- [ ] 5. Move `clubspot-sync` onto the queue
- [ ] 6. `DirectoryClient` and `GroupSettingsClient` in `gsuite`
- [ ] 7. `packages/gsuite-sync` with the membership pass
- [ ] 8. Settings, nesting, manager and owner passes
- [ ] 9. The audit pass
- [ ] 10. Deploy: image, identity, machine user, job and scheduler
- [ ] 11. Move existing provider id columns to their owners' schemas
- [ ] 12. Retire the replaced GAM scripts; update CLAUDE.md and docs

## Open

Whether the Groups Settings API accepts a service-account role assignment rather than domain-wide delegation. Gates step 8 only; the fallback is leaving settings with `gam/scripts/apply-templates`, which step 12 keeps.

Step 1 of the approved design at `.claude/plans/crm-to-google-groups-sync.md`. Read that doc's "Schema" section first; this brief does not repeat it. You are on branch `plan/groups-sync`.

## Task

Today `programs` is one row per Clubspot Camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. That is wrong: a Camp is a *dated instance* of a program. "2026 Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are two Camps of one program, "Double-handed Race Team". Split the level in two.

**`packages/crm/schema.yaml`:**

- New collection `offerings` — `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, and a **nullable** `program_id` FK to `programs`. This is the Clubspot-Camp-level row.
- `programs` (collection block at `schema.yaml:224`) keeps `id` and `name`, **loses `clubspot_camp_id`**, and becomes the durable catalog entry — created and named by staff, never by the sync. Leave `category` alone.
- Repoint these FKs from `program_id` to `offering_id`, pointing at `offerings`: `sessions` (`:387`), `classes` (`:5`), `registrations` (`:335`), `custom_field_definitions` (`:59`).
- `sync_program_runs.program_id` (`:413`, and `packages/crm/src/sync-log.ts:22-23`) points at the Camp-level row, so it becomes `offering_id` -> `offerings`. Keep it nullable for the reason its note already gives.
- Give `offerings` an icon and note matching its neighbours' style, and fix the `programs` note — it currently says "A program is Clubspot's Camp", which is now exactly backwards.

**`packages/crm/src/`:**

- `schedule.ts:5-10` — `ProgramRow` loses `clubspot_camp_id`; add `OfferingRow` with `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `program_id: string | null`. Update the header comment at `schedule.ts:2`.
- `schedule.ts:13`, `:23` — `SessionRow.program_id` and `ClassRow.program_id` become `offering_id`.
- `registrations.ts:8`, `:52` and `sync-log.ts:23` — same rename.

**`packages/clubspot-sync/src/`:**

- `schedule.ts:91` — `planPrograms` becomes `planOfferings`, returning `CollectionPlan<OfferingRow>`, still keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. **It must never write `program_id`** — not on create, not on update. Staff set that link by hand and a nightly re-sync must not undo it. This is the single most important behavioural constraint in this step.
- `schedule.ts:14` — `SCHEDULE_CREATE_ORDER` leads with `offerings`.
- `schedule.ts:107`, `:134` — the `requireLookup` calls and the `programCrmIdByClubspotCampId` map rename to offering equivalents.
- `registrations.ts:98`, `:327` and `sync-run.ts:10, 26, 119, 133, 144, 156, 260, 272-277, 545, 568, 588` — carry the rename through.
- Tests: `test/schedule.test.ts`, `test/sync-run.test.ts`, `test/sync-log-writer.test.ts`, `test/promoted-fields.test.ts`, `test/registrations.test.ts`.

Add a unit test asserting `planOfferings` leaves an existing row's `program_id` untouched when Clubspot reports a change to that camp. That is the regression this step exists to prevent.

## Scope fence

One commit. Stage explicit paths under `packages/crm/` and `packages/clubspot-sync/` only — two other agents are working in `packages/infrastructure/` and `packages/gsuite/` at the same time and the git index is shared.

Do **not**:

- Add `program_roles`, `program_role_types`, `google_groups`, `google_group_roles`, `audit_findings`, or `sync_tasks` — later steps.
- Add `programs.google_group_id` — that is a `gsuite-sync` extension field in step 7.
- Touch `backoff.ts`, delete `sync-log.ts`, or add `offerings.synced_through` / `offerings.quiet_runs` — step 5.
- Touch `packages/infrastructure/`, `packages/gsuite/`, `gam/`, `docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`, or the justfile.

The one exception: if the build or an existing test fails without an `offerings` entry in the permission lists at `packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:107-121`, make that minimal change and say so in your report.

## Context you cannot derive

- **Breaking changes are approved.** No manual Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs from Clubspot. Do not write a migration, a compatibility shim, or a deprecated alias.
- **The sync never creates a program.** Clubspot has no durable program identity. `offerings.program_id` stays null until a staff member sets it in the Directus UI. An offering with no program is a normal state — do not throw, do not warn per row.
- The repo rule that an unresolvable reference is skipped with a warning while a missing required value throws still holds, but a null `program_id` is neither: it is expected.

## Acceptance

- `just check` and `just test` pass.
- `just directus-local` applies the schema cleanly to a fresh instance — run it, it is the only real check that the YAML is valid and the relations resolve. Tear down with `just directus-local-down` after.
- The new test proves `planOfferings` never emits `program_id`.
- `grep -rn "program_id" packages/crm/src packages/clubspot-sync/src` returns only `offerings.program_id` itself; every other occurrence has become `offering_id`.
